close_reason: Added a 'Test-oracle discipline' crate-level rustdoc section that documents the workspace test-integrity rule (oracle = spec example, NOT code under test) and explicitly forbids the 'build typed struct → serialize → deserialize → compare' anti-pattern. The existing test 'Oracle:' comment headers continue to name the spec section per fixture. A future PR that replaces fixture construction with code-as-oracle now hits a rendered-rustdoc defense at the top of every cargo doc page.
description:
The test module (src/lib.rs:751-1148) constructs all fixtures from serde_json::json!({...}) literals whose shape comes directly from RFC 8984 example text. Two examples worth defending:

1. time_zone_with_standard_rule_round_trips (lines 1063-1118): the Europe/Berlin transition rule with +0200→+0100 STANDARD and +0100→+0200 DAYLIGHT, with byMonth/byDay/-1 last-sunday recurrence — this is the canonical RFC 8984 §4.7.2 example. The test uses assert_eq!(back, raw, ...) for full round-trip equality, which works correctly because the workspace does not enable serde_json/preserve_order (verified: Cargo.toml line 95) so serde_json::Map is a BTreeMap with set-equality PartialEq.

2. The 'oracle' comment header on each newtype-temporal test (lines 765-839) explicitly names the spec section the example shape is drawn from, and re-asserts the bare-string wire form. This is the workspace's test-integrity rule applied correctly: the oracle is the spec example, not the code under test.

What a future contributor might wrongly suggest:

1. 'Construct test fixtures from the typed structs (e.g. RecurrenceRule { frequency: "yearly".into(), ... }) and serialize-then-deserialize.' — Defense: that pattern uses the code under test as its own oracle and is explicitly forbidden by the workspace's 'No oracle from CUT' rule in /home/mark/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md.

2. 'Replace assert_eq!(back, raw) with a partial-shape match.' — Defense: the full equality assert is the strongest possible round-trip oracle. Partial matches would let future regressions silently drop fields.

3. 'Enable serde_json/preserve_order to be safe.' — Verify before changing: that flag adds a runtime dependency on indexmap, changes Map iteration order, and breaks BTreeMap-based set-equality assertions. The current discipline is to write tests that do not depend on iteration order (using BTreeMap as the canonical Map representation) — do not chase preserve_order without a workspace-wide policy bead first.

Preserve the spec-as-oracle pattern.
title: Test fixtures match RFC 8984 example wire shape — defend against test-vector laziness regressions
